verdict_summary: For the eight separate frozen domains, the round-three executable certificate is sound for its advertised finite contract, and every round-one/round-two Scope B blocker is resolved by fresh independent execution, not by author assertion. I reran the exact final validator (validate.py 25805ad1, common.py c4d3c0b1, suite.py e2348453, schema.json b1c062ae) into a private root: 8/8 baselines accept, 531/531 controls (481 reject, 50 accept) and 2/2 infrastructure checks match their intended disposition and exact stage, row-for-row identical to the author's credited candidate. Every native-stage rejection is backed by the raw ELF outcome (114 equality-assertion panics at oracle_family_exact.rs:44, 18 parse-unwrap Err panics at :35), and mirrored aggregate corruptions reach the native aggregate-product predicate only after faithfulness and cross-equality pass. Independent mathematics with my own parser and canonical form reproduces all domain counts, definition tables, the 16 CT and 240 YM even-f nonliteral pairs, the aggregate factorization of every graph/route/mode without distribution, every per-owner port permutation, CT provenance and the None/Auto mapping. 68 new semantic held-outs plus 4 infrastructure cases (all predictions matched, except one test-design error of mine) show that every validator predicate is reachable and correct. There is no ELF-side symbol pre-registration, and license failures cannot masquerade as parse errors or inequality. No blocking finding. Six nonblocking findings: interface presence and typed-port order are not bound (cross-route by design; also not by the anchor layer); pool-1/Run metadata is unconsumed; ports-vs-expression typing and locality are capture-bound; a hypothetical result-file classification nuance; uneven suite predicate coverage; and the exercised mapping count. All six need only limits/wording (or optional binding), no theorem, expectation or production change.
